results.content: And I think you said, Alberto, if inflation comes down, what are you going to talk about next year? Given that the market is dominated by the price-sensitive buyers, who get to have a higher risk premium, I don't think we are at a tipping point. **Graf:** I'm going to finish before I go to audience questions, and I'll grab the laptop here in a second, but Elliot, if you can talk a little bit about the dollar. I do think that given the expectation that rates are likely to remain higher longer, certainly in the US, and Lee will talk about this also, is that there is a hunt for assets that in expectation give you higher yield and higher return in private, so private markets becomes the logical choice. So what that tells you is the market has become very attuned to what is happening on the fiscal side, and I think that is going to result absolutely in higher volatility, and potentially higher risk premium, return premium.
